COBIT 2019 — governance objectives and Managed Data (COBIT 2019 (EDM01-05,
One assessment, four vocabularies. These are not four independent measurements — they are one evidence base expressed in four published
frameworks. The four overall figures landing close together is the correct result: the same answers, projected through the same eleven capability
pillars. What differs between them is emphasis and structure, which is what makes each one legible to a different audience.
Retained share is how much of the framework’s own definition of a dimension is in scope under this engagement’s layer. Scored share is how
much of what is in scope was actually measured. They answer different questions and are never combined: a dimension can be fully retained
and barely scored, or the reverse, and a single "coverage" number would hide whichever is worse.
All figures are on the DGIW 1-5 maturity scale. They are NOT rescaled to each framework’s own scale — DCAM scores 1-6 and COBIT 2019
uses capability levels 0-5. A DCAM component shown here as 3.2 is 3.2 out of 5, not out of 6.
What is published and what is ours
Framework names, codes and dimension structures are published content. The relative WEIGHTS applied to those dimensions
are Godaitec editorial judgement — none of these four frameworks publishes weightings for its own dimensions. The weights are
the first thing to challenge in review, and changing them changes every figure derived from them.
COBIT2019 (COBIT 2019 (EDM01-05, APO14)) — Published structure recorded at MEDIUM confidence — verify before relying on it in an audit
The five EDM governance objectives are high confidence, including EDM05 'Ensured Stakeholder Engagement' (renamed from COBIT 5's
'Ensure Stakeholder Transparency'). APO14 Managed Data was new in COBIT 2019 and carries ten management practices
APO14.01-APO14.10. The titles below were originally paraphrased from memory; they have since been checked against a public COBIT
2019 reference and two were corrected (APO14.03 lost a stray 'the', APO14.08 now reads 'life cycle' as two words). They have NOT been
checked against the ISACA publication itself, which is the only source an audit function should accept — that verification is still outstanding
and is why structureConfidence stays at medium rather than rising. COBIT 2019 capability levels run 0-5, which is why scaleMin is 0 and not
1. Giving APO14 55% of the framework weight is DGIW's judgement: it is the only data-specific objective in COBIT, so a COBIT-framed DATA
assessment cannot sensibly be dominated by the generic governance domain.

Why each dimension maps to the capabilities it does
Every row below was authored deliberately. A mapping a consultant cannot defend in a room is not a mapping, and this section is the room.
EDM01 · Ensured Governance Framework Setting and Maintenance
Setting and maintaining the governance framework is the definition of P01.
EDM01 requires the framework to be aligned to enterprise objectives, which is P02.
Benefits delivery is the business case and its realisation — P02.
For a data programme, benefit is overwhelmingly realised at the consumption end, P11.
Data risk in COBIT terms is dominated by security, privacy and regulatory exposure — P08.
Risk appetite is set and monitored by the governance body, P01.
Poor data quality is itself an operational risk that EDM03 expects to be optimised, P05.
BCBS 239 makes risk data aggregation a lineage problem: a bank must show how a risk number was
derived. Banking-only, so EDM03 retains 0.80 under core.
Resource optimisation for data is predominantly platform and tooling efficiency, P10.
People are the scarce resource in data governance — steward time allocation is P01.
Resourcing decisions follow from the funding strategy, P02.

Stakeholder engagement and transparency of governance reporting are operating-model capabilities,
EDM05 is also about communicating value and direction to stakeholders, which is P02.
APO14.01 · Define and communicate the data management strategy, roles and
APO14.01 is explicitly the data management strategy — P02.
The same practice defines roles and responsibilities, which is P01.
APO14.02 · Define and maintain a consistent business glossary
A consistent business glossary is P04's central artefact. A clean one-to-one.
APO14.03 · Establish processes and infrastructure for metadata management
This practice names infrastructure explicitly — the catalogue tooling — which DGIW holds in P10.
APO14.04 · Define a data quality strategy
A data quality strategy is P05.
In a regulated bank the quality strategy has to state how accuracy is evidenced to source.
Banking-only, so APO14.04 retains 0.85 under core.
Fixture Bank Limited — Framework Alignment — COBIT2019
APO14.05 · Establish data profiling methodologies, processes and tools
Profiling methodology is quality practice, P05.
The practice names tools explicitly; profiling capability is bounded by the platform, P10.
APO14.06 · Ensure a data quality assessment approach
A quality assessment approach maps wholly onto P05.
APO14.07 · Define the data cleansing approach
Cleansing is remediation, the closing half of the quality cycle P05 measures.
In practice most cleansing effort is deduplication and survivorship on master data, P06.
APO14.08 · Manage the life cycle of data assets
Managing the lifecycle of data assets is P09's subject.
Lifecycle stages have to be designed into the architecture to be enforceable, P03.
APO14.09 · Support data archiving and retention
Archiving and retention is P09. A clean one-to-one.
Fixture Bank Limited — Framework Alignment — COBIT2019
APO14.10 · Manage data backup and restore arrangements
Backup and restore is an operational platform capability, P10.
Restore windows are set by retention obligations, which P09 measures.

What this assessment does not cover
Every leaf dimension of COBIT2019 is both in scope under this layer and measured. Nothing in the framework is unaddressed.
DCAM is modelled at v2.2. Its capability and sub-capability levels beneath each component are deliberately NOT authored: they were not
recalled reliably enough to put in front of an auditor, and an absent level is recoverable where an invented one is not. DCAM v3.0
reorganised the model and is not what is represented here.
COBIT 2019 APO14 sub-practice titles have been checked against a public COBIT 2019 reference and corrected where they differed. They
have NOT been checked against the ISACA publication itself, which is the only source an audit function should accept — treat them as
verified secondhand, not as quoted. The five EDM governance objectives are high confidence.
The three DGI groupings used as parents are how the published DGI diagram arranges the ten components; treating that arrangement as a
formal level is a modelling choice, not published hierarchy.
